title: Per-state election event inventory
description: The frontend-readable catalogue of which election events exist for each state. The backend's events.py registry is the source of truth at backend-build time; this JSON is the static-app view, hand-authored and kept consistent via CI test (backend/tests/test_election_events_consistency.py). Per-state arrays let route components resolve `defaultEventForState(stateCode)` without bundling Python. National events (e.g. LsGenApr2024) appear in every relevant state's array as a 'slice' — same event_id, same artifact directory, the per-state read just selects the right row. Per ADR-0023.

x-changelog.description: Initial schema. Per-state event inventory keyed by ECI state code. Each event entry: event_id, kind (assembly/parliament/by_election; the parliament kind was named `lok_sabha` in v1.0 / v1.1), display, polled_on, optional default flag (at most one default per state — defines what /s/<state>/elections resolves to).

Breaking: removed the `default` boolean property. The per-state default event is now derived from `max(polled_on)` in `defaultEventForState()` (frontend/src/lib/election-events.ts) and in the backend's election-events Parquet writer; the hand-authored flag was a shadow of a computable fact and backfills routinely forgot to set it, causing Meghalaya/Tripura/UP/etc. to fall through to the rows[0] = oldest-event fallback. PR #191 fixed the rendering by making polled_on canonical; this PR retires the now-dead field across the schema, the 23 on-disk entries, the Pydantic seed (`_Event.default`, `is_default` Parquet column, the at-most-one-default raise), and the Tier-A test `test_election_events_default_uniqueness`. Adapter and reader code that touched `default` was updated in the same commit; readers that ignored the field are unaffected. See ADR-0023 §latest and TODO/20260524-elections-topic-and-default-cleanup-plan.md (if filed) for the full rationale.

MINOR additive on the consumer side, rename within the kind enum: `lok_sabha` -> `parliament`. Per the PR-0 No-Hindi policy locked in docs/architecture/frontend/url-grammar.md section No-Hindi policy (PR-0 2026-06-09), the kind enum now uses the English noun `parliament` for the national lower-house cohort. Citizen chrome, code identifiers, URL slugs, and the kind enum are all English-only after this PR (PR-W1a of TODO/20260609-election-experience-overhaul-plan.md). The publisher-verbatim attribution titles in datasets/data/entities/source.csv (`General Election to Lok Sabha YYYY ...`) are preserved as a documented carve-out: those titles feed datasets/schemas/source.schema.json + backend.yen_gov.canonical.citation.derive_source_id (SHA-stable identity per ADR-0032 / ADR-0042); changing them would re-derive every src-* id and break FK closure across the 36 per-state election_results.csv shards. The kind enum and chrome strings carry the English noun; the publisher-credit titles remain verbatim. Description prose on `kind`, `display`, `term_end_estimated`, and `notes` is updated in lock-step. Consumer datasets/taxonomy/election_events.json stamp bumped 1.1 -> 1.2 to satisfy the Tier-B `$schema_version == x-version` invariant.

Additive: extend kind enum with `general_bye` + `assembly_bye` per the PR-0 bye-slug doctrine locked in docs/architecture/frontend/url-grammar.md (event-slug grammar `assembly-bye-<YYYY>-<seat-slug>` and `general-bye-<YYYY>-<state-slug>-<seat-slug>`); add optional `event_id_aliases: string[]` field carrying legacy event_id values for one-release readability of pre-W2a bookmarks and stored data (rows in datasets/data/datapoints/electoral/*.csv still carry the cohort-format period_label values, resolved back to the renamed event_id via this alias array). Widen the event_id pattern from `^[A-Za-z0-9]+$` to `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` so the new citizen-readable slugs (`general-2024`, `assembly-2024`, `assembly-bye-2024-channapatna`) validate; the old cohort-format ids (`LsGenJun2024`, `AcGenMay2026`) still match the widened pattern. After W3+ surfaces flip to the new slug, event_id_aliases becomes a curiosity and eventual deletion is a Phase 5+ concern. See PR-W2a row in TODO/20260609-election-experience-overhaul-plan.md.

sources.description: Provenance per CLAUDE.md §12 / ADR-0002. Empty array signals hand-authored content (the canonical case here — this file mirrors backend/yen_gov/sources/eci/events.py, validated by CI consistency test).

states.description: Map from ECI state code (e.g. S22, U07) to a chronological list (most recent first) of election events for which our datasets/elections/ tree contains parsed data. States with NO election data on disk are omitted entirely; the loader returns an empty array for them, which the UI renders as 'no election data ingested yet'.

event_id.description: Citizen-readable event identifier: `general-<YYYY>` for national Parliament (the state slice of an all-India event), `assembly-<YYYY>` for the state assembly, `assembly-bye-<YYYY>-<seat-slug>` for an assembly by-election (state is in the URL path), `general-bye-<YYYY>-<state-slug>-<seat-slug>` for a national by-election. The pre-W2a cohort-format ids (`LsGenJun2024`, `AcGenMay2026`, `LsByeJan2021`, `AcByeDec2019`) are preserved in `event_id_aliases[]` for one-release readability of legacy bookmarks and stored data (the cohort form is still the on-disk period_label in datasets/data/datapoints/electoral/*.csv, which the alias array maps back to this id). The backend's events.py registry retains the cohort form internally as the write-time period_label tied to parse_period_label; the alias bridges the two surfaces. See PR-W2a row in TODO/20260609-election-experience-overhaul-plan.md and the bye-slug grammar in docs/architecture/frontend/url-grammar.md.

event_id_aliases.description: Legacy event_id values that ALSO resolve to this row. Strangler-fig for one release cycle: covers (a) old bookmarks (a citizen who saved `/state/elections/LsGenJun2024` before W2a still finds the right page), (b) write-time identifiers persisted in `datasets/data/datapoints/electoral/*.csv` `period_label` values which are still in cohort form (the backend's parse_period_label contract makes them invariant for now). After W3+ surfaces flip to the renamed slug and the per-row aliases are no longer queried, this array becomes a curiosity; eventual deletion is a Phase 5+ concern.

kind.description: Political body and event-type the event elected. 'assembly' = state assembly (the citizen's primary state government), event_id `assembly-<YYYY>`; 'parliament' = national lower-house cohort (the state's MPs sent to Delhi - kept separate per the cause/consequence doctrine in ADR-0023, never co-mingled with assembly results), event_id `general-<YYYY>`; 'assembly_bye' = single-seat assembly by-election, event_id `assembly-bye-<YYYY>-<seat-slug>` (state is in URL path); 'general_bye' = single-seat Parliament by-election, event_id `general-bye-<YYYY>-<state-slug>-<seat-slug>`; 'by_election' = pre-W2a legacy kind retained for backwards-compatibility with any catalogue rows that have not yet been classified into the more specific assembly_bye / general_bye kinds. The 'parliament' value was named `lok_sabha` in v1.0 / v1.1; renamed in v1.2 per the PR-0 No-Hindi policy locked at docs/architecture/frontend/url-grammar.md. The `general_bye` + `assembly_bye` kinds were added in v1.3 per the PR-0 bye-slug doctrine.

display.description: Citizen-facing label. Cohort codes (e.g. AcGenJun2024) MUST NOT appear in this string — citizens think in (state, year), not ECI cohort artifact. Format guideline: '<State> Assembly · <Month YYYY>' or '<State> · Parliament <YYYY>'.

polled_on.description: Polling date (or last polling date for multi-phase events). Drives the recency rule in StateOverview (election leads <90d post-poll, otherwise government-card leads). For multi-state cohorts polling on different days, this is the state-specific date.

term_end_estimated.description: Estimated term-end (typically polled_on + 5 years per Article 172). Null for Parliament slices and by-elections. Used to surface 'next election due' chrome in the final year of term.

data_status.description: Tells the UI what to expect on disk. 'complete' = full result.summary.json + per-AC results emitted (the ingested case); 'partial' = some artifacts present (rare); 'pending_upstream' = ECI has not yet published (e.g. Bihar 2025), UI surfaces an honest 'awaiting publication' message rather than a 404.

notes.description: Optional context for citizen-facing display (e.g. 'Held concurrently with Parliament 2024').
